plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium strategy is to bid a fraction (n-1)/n = 2/3 of my value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $47, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 × 47 ≈ $31.3 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard symmetric equilibrium bid shading factor for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $33, so I'll bid approximately 33 * (2/3) ≈ 22 to balance winning probability against overpaying, maximizing expected profit given rational competitors likely bidding similarly.

With values uniformly distributed on [0,49] and 3 bidders total, the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3, assuming symmetric equilibrium strategies. Given my value of $36, I'll bid approximately 2/3 of my value to balance winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while staying competitive against Andy and Betty's likely similar bidding strategies.
